args.rationale: Applying the firm's hearsay memo (FRE 801 test) to Scenario B of the Meridian Grain Cooperative client letter. Under Section 1 of the memo, hearsay requires both (a) an out-of-court statement and (b) that it is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Scenario B is Ms. Kite's out-of-court remark ('the north silo fan has been shorting for weeks') made at the February vendor meeting. However, the client letter's controlling stated purpose is expressly not to prove the truth of the remark. The client states it does not care whether the remark was accurate and is offering it solely to show the effect on the listener — that Ms. Vosniak was on notice and had a duty to inspect. Under Section 3(a) of the memo, an out-of-court statement offered for effect on the listener (notice/warning) is a recognized non-hearsay purpose, and Section 4 requires taking the client's stated purpose as controlling and not inventing an alternative. Because the item is offered for a non-truth (notice) purpose, the hearsay test is not satisfied. The item is therefore NOT hearsay, so the determination is rejected.
